subject: english2
stem: A passage argues that short, repeated study sessions are more effective than long, infrequent ones. What is the author's main point?

options.text: Long study sessions are always a waste of time.
Consistent repetition improves retention more reliably.
Workers should study only on weekends.
Memory depends mainly on natural talent.

explanation: 题干已经给出作者强调 repeated study sessions，更符合主旨的是 consistent repetition improves retention。

subject: english2
stem: If a paragraph states that digital notes are useful only when reviewed regularly, what can be inferred?

options.text: Taking notes alone does not guarantee learning.
Paper notes are always better.
Reviewing notes is unnecessary.
Digital tools reduce all forgetting.

explanation: only when reviewed regularly 说明单纯记笔记不够，关键在复盘，所以选 A。

subject: english2
stem: A line says, 'The schedule looked efficient on paper but failed in practice.' Which option best explains the failure?

options.text: The plan ignored real-world execution constraints.
The paper quality was poor.
The schedule was too short to print.
Practice is less important than design.

explanation: on paper but failed in practice 常指纸面方案没有考虑实际执行约束，所以选 A。

subject: english2
stem: A text says that busy learners improve more when they study every day for 15 minutes than when they study once a week for two hours. Which statement best supports this idea?

options.text: Regular exposure helps memory stay active.
Long sessions are easier to schedule.
Weekly study reduces all stress.
Learning depends mostly on mood.

explanation: 题干强调短时高频更有效，A 直接解释了原因：规律接触能让记忆持续活跃。

subject: english2
stem: If an author mentions that a chart looks impressive but hides missing data, the author's attitude toward the chart is most likely ______.

options.text: fully trusting
carefully critical
openly excited
completely indifferent

explanation: looks impressive but hides missing data 表示作者有保留并带有批判性，所以选 carefully critical。

subject: english2
stem: A sentence says, 'The tool saves time only after users learn to use it properly.' What does this suggest?

options.text: The tool is useless in every situation.
Training affects whether the tool becomes efficient.
Time savings come immediately for everyone.
Users should avoid new tools.

explanation: only after users learn to use it properly 说明工具是否高效取决于是否掌握使用方法。

subject: english2
stem: A passage introduces a problem, then compares two solutions, and finally recommends one. Which reading strategy is most useful here?

options.text: Ignore the structure and focus on vocabulary only.
Track how the author organizes ideas and shifts stance.
Translate every sentence before reading the question.
Memorize the first paragraph and skip the last.

explanation: 题干强调文章结构是“问题-比较-推荐”，最有效的是跟踪结构与作者态度变化。

subject: english2
stem: If a writer says that a method is popular but unsupported by solid evidence, what is the writer mainly warning readers against?

options.text: Using any new method at work
Believing claims just because they are common
Reading evidence too carefully
Making unpopular choices

explanation: popular but unsupported by solid evidence 的重点是提醒读者不要因为常见就轻信。

subject: english2
stem: A writer says that efficient learners stop trying to memorize everything and instead focus on what is most reusable. What is the writer's advice?

options.text: Learn fewer things, but choose high-value material.
Avoid reviewing old content.
Memorize all examples in every text.
Study only when exams are close.

explanation: focus on what is most reusable 的核心意思就是优先高价值内容，而不是面面俱到。

subject: english2
stem: If a passage notes that people remember corrections better when they make the original mistake themselves, what does this imply about learning?

options.text: Passive reading is always enough.
Error-based feedback can deepen memory.
Mistakes should be hidden from learners.
Correct answers are less useful than wrong ones.

explanation: 题干强调亲自犯错后再纠正更容易记住，说明基于错误的反馈会加深记忆。

subject: english2
stem: An author describes a method as 'practical, though not elegant.' Which attitude is closest to the author's?

options.text: Mild approval despite some reservation
Complete rejection
Strong emotional attachment
Total confusion

explanation: practical 表示认可，though not elegant 表示保留，所以是带保留的认可。

subject: english2
stem: A paragraph moves from a common belief to a research finding that challenges it. What should readers pay most attention to?

options.text: The date of the paragraph
The shift point where the author's stance changes
The number of long words
Whether the belief is popular online

explanation: 从常见看法切到研究发现，关键就是抓住 stance change 的转折点。

subject: english2
stem: A passage argues that busy professionals learn better when they reduce decision fatigue before studying. What is the practical suggestion?

options.text: Prepare the study task in advance so starting requires less choice.
Study only when completely free from work.
Avoid using any schedule.
Spend more time choosing materials than studying them.

explanation: reduce decision fatigue 的实操方式就是提前准备任务，降低开始前的选择成本。

subject: english2
stem: If the author says a popular study method is 'appealing but shallow,' what is the most likely meaning?

options.text: It looks attractive, but its learning effect may be limited.
It is hard to understand and highly technical.
It has been carefully tested for years.
It should replace all older methods immediately.

explanation: appealing but shallow 表示看起来吸引人，但深度和效果不足。

subject: english2
stem: A text states that 'progress becomes visible only after many invisible repetitions.' What is the writer emphasizing?

options.text: Real improvement often depends on repeated practice that feels ordinary.
Visible progress is unimportant.
Repetition should be avoided because it is boring.
Only talented learners can improve.

explanation: 句子强调大量看似普通、不可见的重复最终形成可见进步。

subject: english2
stem: The author compares a study plan to a map rather than a promise. What does this comparison suggest?

options.text: A plan guides action but may still need adjustment.
A plan guarantees success if written neatly.
Maps are less useful than promises.
Study plans should never change.

explanation: map 强调引导方向，而不是保证结果，说明计划需要边走边调。

subject: english2
stem: A paragraph mentions that learners often confuse familiarity with mastery. Which warning is the author most likely giving?

options.text: Recognizing material is not the same as being able to use it.
Learners should avoid all repeated content.
Mastery depends only on memory speed.
Familiarity is always more important than practice.

explanation: familiarity 与 mastery 混淆，核心警告就是“看着眼熟”不等于“真正掌握”。

subject: english2
stem: If a writer introduces three examples and then says 'all of them point to the same lesson,' what should readers expect next?

options.text: A summary statement connecting the examples
A list of unrelated numbers
A change to a completely new topic
An argument against using examples

explanation: all point to the same lesson 之后通常会出现总括句，把前面例子统一起来。

subject: english2
stem: A study article says that measuring the right thing matters more than measuring everything. Which choice best reflects this idea?

options.text: Useful indicators should be selective and tied to the goal.
More data always guarantees better decisions.
Measurement should be avoided because it creates pressure.
Only experts should look at progress data.

explanation: 题干强调不是全测，而是测对目标真正有意义的指标。

subject: english2
stem: If a passage notes that a learner improved only after shortening each study session, the author is most likely emphasizing ______.

options.text: the value of manageable study units
the need to stop studying every day
the danger of all long-term planning
the uselessness of repetition

explanation: shortening each session 后效果反而提升，强调的是可执行、可持续的小单元学习。
